name: International Space Station
description: Low Earth orbit, about 420 km up (approximate). Earth's magnetic field blocks most solar particles, so the solar particle factor is low. Mission control leads medical decisions and replies within seconds.

name: Lunar transit spacecraft
description: Crew capsule in cislunar space between Earth and the Moon, roughly 250,000 km from Earth on average (approximate; it changes along the trajectory). Zero gravity, a small cabin and thin shielding outside Earth's magnetic field. The storm shelter is a corner of the cabin walled with crew stowage bags (assumption). Medical decisions are shared between the crew and mission control with a signal delay of about 1 second one way (approximate).

name: Lunar surface base
description: Surface base about 384,400 km from Earth (approximate). The base structure gives some shielding, but there is no magnetic field shield. Medical decisions are shared between the crew and mission control.

name: Pressurized lunar rover
description: Crew in a pressurized rover on a multi-day traverse, about 50 km from the lunar base (approximate), so roughly 384,450 km from Earth. Lunar gravity (0.166 g, same as the surface base) and thin hull shielding. Return to the base takes hours to a day or two; the evacuation time shown is to Earth care (approximate). The crew leads medical decisions and consults mission control when needed (signal delay about 1.3 seconds one way).

name: Mars mission
description: Transit toward Mars. Average distance about 225 million km (approximate; it changes with orbital position). One-way signal delay can reach about 22 minutes. The crew leads medical decisions. Gravity is set to 0 for transit (assumption).
